pr_body:
On some systems (Win 10), localhost resolves to ::1 first, creating
a sub-par development experience when connecting to localhost by
introducing a 300-500ms delay on connection.

Fixes https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/1022.

> lookup what localhost is, and then call .listen() on that address.

@mcollina Did I miss something?
@StarpTech that's what Node.js core would do. If you specify `localhost` it looks up in the OS what ip address that matches to. Then it listen to that address.
@mcollina great, it sounded like a todo for us.
Is the issue that the app is listening on 127.0.0.1 but the actual request is created like `curl http://localhost:8000/foo` which causes Windows to timeout on IPv6 first?

I think this makes things too ambiguous. With this solution we are trying to solve for the idiosyncrasies of OSes when that isn't our problem. I think a simple note advising people to use `http://127.0.01...`, or specify their own bind address, is the appropriate solution.

That being said, I won't block this if you guys think this is best.
I think this provides a better user experience on Windows. If there is pushback/bugs opened about this we could revisit later.

I know it's been a couple years since this change (which has since been [moved into server.js](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/2af8a3ceae2e498a664e9865f31920bd987e8ca2/lib/server.js#L66)), but I just wanted to say that it doesn't actually do what was intended. This PR assumes that by feeding `localhost` to `Server.listen` the server will be listening on the IPv6 loopback address `::1` on Windows (or any system where the OS returns an IPv6 address before an IPv4 address for `localhost`). However, this is not currently the case. `Server.listen` [delegates host resolution to `dns.lookup`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/87805375645f7af36fce2e59289559f746a7131d/lib/net.js#L1487-L1495), without giving it any extra options. When used in this manner, `dns.lookup` will always return an IPv4 address, even if the operating system returns an IPv6 address first. In order to get the addresses in OS order, a `{ verbatim: true }` [flag needs to be passed to `dns.lookup`](https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v14.x/docs/api/dns.html#dns_dns_lookup_hostname_options_callback).

I'm not convinced, however, that listening _only_ on the IPv6 loopback is a good solution, as it will mean that accessing the server using a more conventional `127.0.0.1` address will not be possible. This can possibly stump many users.

For comparison, `express` defaults to listening on the wildcard address, which avoids the original issue entirely. Of course, this comes with the cost of exposing the server to outside access without the developer explicitly asking for it.
@dmitri-gb would you mind opening an issue with your great analysis to track this use case?

> @Eomm how about reopening [the original issue](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/1022)?

It is quite old. A new issue would be better. Referencing the old one would be okay.

issue_context.title: Strange behavior at first call and after 5s
issue_context.body:
#### Context

* *node version*: 10.0.0
* *fastify version*: ^1.6.0

Hi,

I'am using fastify through a small nestjs project. I have a single GET REST method. 

Using Fastify, the first call takes 500ms at minimum and if I continue calling the same method, the response time falls arround 4ms.

BUT, if I wait 5 seconds between 2 calls, the second call replies after 500ms again.

I do not see this problem using Express.

Anyone else experienced this behavior?

Thank you
comments: Can you please include a snippet to reproduce your problem?
Closing due to inactivity, feel free to reopen!
I'm not able to reproduce this under macOS. @StarpTech can you try this?
I've tried on another teammate computer, also on windows10 but under nodeJS v8.x and he has the same behavior (with fiddler4 client).

I cannot reproduce this on Windows either. Might it be some antivirus/firewall? It might also be a client issue, have you tried with postman?

We disconnect keepalive connections after 5s.

I have the same behavior with fiddler4 and postman. I also disabled my firewall. Still the same behavior.

So it seems to be the 5s timeout on keep-alive connections that is the cause of this problem?

@cabrinoob do you experience the same thing with Chrome? Can you check with Node 10.6.0 if it has the same issue? We inherit that behavior from Node.js core, see https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_server_keepalivetimeout.

Does Node 8 has the same problem?
Does Node 8 has the same issue?

I am experiencing this as well with node 8 (my own project, similar scope):
 
node v8.9.0
Windows 10 both on WSL and native.
Chrome, Firefox and Insomnia as REST clients.

Going to test later under Linux because as long as it doesn't happen there it's a moot point for me.

Does this happens with https://github.com/fastify/benchmarks/blob/master/benchmarks/bare.js?

I cannot reproduce this at all.
@mcollina : using `bare.js` I cannot see the problem. I have some fluctuations between 2ms and 20ms, but nothing compared to the gap 2ms - 500ms observed with fastify.

Unfortunately I cannot reproduce on Windows, Linux or Mac OS X. It seems very much system dependent.

I'll be happy to review a PR that fixes this problem (if it's a problem with fastify).

I cam reproduce this issue with the minimal fastify example posted here by @cabrinoob but the issue is not reproducible by the bare.js posted by mcollina. This is the case whether I'm using WSL or Windows (have not tested under Linux, doing this next) 

This leads me to believe it must be an issue with fastify. Not sure if it is or not but them both behaving different seems indicative of an issue in one but not the other.

Can you reproduce it with https://github.com/fastify/benchmarks/blob/master/benchmarks/fastify.js?
(no async await)

@delvedor : Yes, I reproduce the 500ms lag with your code.

I'll try to put it on a docker image and call it under linux to see if I can reproduce this behavior
@delvedor I will try to reproduce it tonight and report.

I can reproduce the problem. If I open `http://localhost:3000` I get the delay. If I open `http://127.0.0.1:3000` I do not get the delay.

@justintime4tea @cabrinoob 

Moreover I can reproduce it with plain core: 

```
'use strict'

const server = require('http').createServer(function (req, res) {
  res.setHeader('content-type', 'application/json')
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ hello: 'world' }))
})

server.listen(3000, '127.0.0.1')
```

Then opening `http://localhost:3000` will have the delay.

It seems that _just_ adding that 2nd property in `.listen()` slows down Windows for some reason.
This looks like a bug on Node.js core on Windows.

Side note, this is triggered by passing in _any_ value.

cc @jsumners
@mcollina You are awesome! Thank you so much for the feedback on this! We're using Linux in production so it's good to know we won't be seeing this in production. Good ol' Winderz >_<

Ok, great!
For the fun, I've just tested with `server.listen(3000)` (without forcing the 127.0.0.1) and make requests with postman on 127.0.0.1 and it works like a charm.

switching on localhost brings up the problem.

Confirmed it's a WIndows problem. The following does not cause the slowdown:

```js
'use strict'

const server = require('http').createServer(function (req, res) {
  res.setHeader('content-type', 'application/json')
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ hello: 'world' }))
})

server.listen(3000, '::1')
```

This is happening because you have IPv6 enabled on your machine, and `localhost` is first resolving to `::1` (`localhost` in IPv6), and _then_ to `127.0.0.1`. On Mac OS X, `localhost` resolves to `127.0.0.1`. I assume this is the same for Linux.

As for solving this bug, I see two possible ways:

1. lookup what `localhost` is, and then call `.listen()` on that address. Some docs will need to be updated, as we will not be bound to IPv4 anymore. Considering this would not affect production deployments, I think we can ship this in a semver-minor.

2. do not listen a specific address at all, but rather to all specific interfaces. This reduces some base security as it will expose the server over the network.

I'm for 1. @fastify/fastify what do you think?
The 1. approach is implemented in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/1047.

As I say in #1047, I think the solution is:

3. Add a note to the documentation explaining that "localhost" usually references multiple addresses which can cause name resolution delays. Fastify explicitly binds to `127.0.0.1`. Thus, to avoid name resolution delays, requests should be made to `http://127.0.0.1...` instead of `http://localhost...`.
Same with Node `v12.16.3` on Windows.
Very likely it’s a different bug or you are doing something odd on your end.

Hi, awesome to land here 😄 I researched for hours. I can reproduce it with Node.js 14.17.2 and the latest 16. I use WSL2 with ubuntu.

Listen to `::1` fix it but `127.0.0.1` or `localhost` produce a delay every 5s for more than 200ms in our servers.
As @jsumners mentioned always request `127.0.0.1` and it works.
